situation:
You are the operations coordinator at NORTHBEAM COFFEE CO., a drive-thru coffee chain with forty locations in two states. Six months ago the company bought MILE POST COFFEE, a smaller drive-thru chain, and the two operations have not been fully joined yet. The district operations manager (judge) has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

Before the purchase, a shift lead at a MILE POST COFFEE store could remake or refund a drink at the window on the spot. The merged company now runs one refund policy: only the store manager enters a refund, and that manager covers three stores and is rarely on site. Shift leads have to interpret that policy to customers at the window themselves.

The morning rush fills a lane to twelve cars before it backs into the street. A sold-out promotional syrup has produced several complaints a shift, and each one stops the lane while a shift lead explains the policy. Nobody passes the delivery schedule to the shift leads, so they cannot tell a customer when the flavour returns. Holding deep backup stock of every promotional syrup would end the stockouts but ties up cash in inventory that spoils before it sells.

Giving shift leads drawer override codes would settle a complaint at the window in seconds, but a code is issued to one person as a routine precaution, and spreading codes across every lead weakens the link between a drawer and the person who opened it. Handing the customer a voucher for a later visit instead keeps the lane moving, but sends the customer away unpaid, and MILE POST COFFEE regulars who expect an immediate fix may not come back.

The district operations manager (judge) wants your view on how much authority a shift lead should carry at the window, and a recommendation the crews can follow during the morning rush. The district operations manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the district operations manager (judge) at NORTHBEAM COFFEE CO. Business background is the same as the situation above. You wrote the single refund policy that came out of the purchase of MILE POST COFFEE, you know the store manager covers three stores, and you have been hearing about stopped lanes every morning. You want the operations coordinator to tell you how much authority a shift lead should carry at the window, and to recommend something the crews can follow during the morning rush.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this to a customer who is still sitting at the window with the wrong drink?
What do we tell the shift leads who used to settle these themselves?
